Claude Code hooks are user-defined commands that run at fixed points in the session lifecycle. The official docs describe them as user-defined shell commands that execute at various points in Claude Code's lifecycle. They are configured in settings files, with ~/.claude/settings.json for user settings and .claude/settings.json for project settings.

Common uses include auto-formatting after edits, blocking risky commands, and notifications. The official guide's examples include formatting files after edits, blocking commands before they execute, and sending notifications when Claude needs input. Hooks are also deterministic: they ensure certain actions always happen rather than relying on the LLM to choose to run them.

Some hooks can send feedback to Claude. If a hook exits with a non-zero status, Claude sees the failure and can adjust its approach. Hook events include PreToolUse and PostToolUse, and one third-party guide lists 30 hook events, though that count is from a secondary source and may be outdated. You can also manage hooks interactively with the `/hooks` command in a session.

Sources are mostly official docs (code.claude.com and docs.anthropic.com) plus third-party tutorials such as DataCamp and Real Python. The official hooks guide is the best place to start.
